# Harrison

## Overview

- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v2 c1 P4](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0004)</sub>
- **Status:** Married  <sub>[v2 c25 P12](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0012), [v2 c25 P59](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0059)</sub>
- **Origin:** New Brunswick (Scottsford)  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057)</sub>
- **Role:** Farmer  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c1 P15](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0015)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** J. A. Harrison  <sub>[v2 c1 P1](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0001), [v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>; James A.  <sub>[v2 c25 P12](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0012), [v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057)</sub>

## Appearance

Mr. Harrison is a short, fat, bald man with prominent blue eyes. Before his wife returned, he wore torn and ragged working clothes and an unkempt beard, but he later shaved his beard, trimmed his hair, and began wearing neatly patched and brushed garments.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P11](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0011), [v2 c25 P46](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0046)_

## Personality

Mr. Harrison is a crabbed, outspoken, and eccentric man who prides himself on telling the blunt truth regardless of others' feelings. Despite his crusty demeanor, he possesses a soft spot for kindred spirits, enjoys lively conversations, and harbors a generous nature when approached in the right manner. He is rather fidgety and set in his habits, preferring a somewhat relaxed standard of house-cleaning compared to his wife's rigorous neatness.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c3 P23](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0023), [v2 c3 P25](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0025), [v2 c3 P49](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0049), [v2 c9 P9](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0009), [v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057)_

## Traits

- Outspoken and blunt  <sub>[v2 c3 P23](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0023), [v2 c3 P25](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0025)</sub>
- Crusty and crabbed  <sub>[v2 c3 P49](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0049)</sub>

- Farming and harvesting  <sub>[v2 c1 P15](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0015), [v2 c6 P7](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0007)</sub>
- Brewing tea  <sub>[v2 c3 P33](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0033)</sub>

## Goals

- To live a quiet life without unnecessary fuss or interference from others  <sub>[v2 c1 P6](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0006), [v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057)</sub>

## History

Mr. Harrison bought the Robert Bell farm next to Green Gables and moved to Avonlea, quickly gaining a reputation as an eccentric bachelor who kept house for himself and owned a swearing parrot named Ginger. He initially clashed with Anne Shirley after her Jersey cow broke into his oatfield, but the two soon became good friends after Anne mistakenly sold his cow and personally came to apologize and make amends. Unknown to his neighbors, Mr. Harrison was actually married to Emily Scott, from whom he had separated due to domestic disagreements over his habits and his parrot. Following an erroneous note in a local newspaper hinting at his impending marriage, his wife arrived in Avonlea to investigate, leading to their reconciliation and her taking charge of his household.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c1 P6](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0006), [v2 c1 P15](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0015), [v2 c2 P35](../source/v02-c02.md#nw-v02-c02-p0035), [v2 c3 P22](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0022), [v2 c3 P39](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0039), [v2 c25 P12](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0012), [v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057), [v2 c25 P59](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0059)_

## Background by volume

- Formerly lived in Scottsford, New Brunswick, before moving to Prince Edward Island  <sub>[v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057)</sub>
- Separated from his wife, Emily, over a dispute involving his profane parrot, Ginger  <sub>[v2 c25 P58](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0058), [v2 c25 P59](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0059)</sub>
- Purchased Robert Bell's farm adjoining Green Gables  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>

## Quotes

> Accidents will happen. I’m too hasty myself sometimes, miss . . . far too hasty. But I can’t help speaking out just what I think and folks must take me as they find me.  <sub>[v2 c3 P23](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0023)</sub>

> I’m a crusty, lonesome, crabbed old chap, but there’s something about that little girl makes me feel young again . . . and it’s such a pleasant sensation I’d like to have it repeated once in a while.  <sub>[v2 c3 P49](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0049)</sub>

> Most paints fade uglier every year but that blue is as ugly as it can be to begin with, so it’s bound to fade prettier.  <sub>[v2 c9 P41](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0041)</sub>

> I suppose I’ll get used to it after awhile but it eases me up to look at the yard. Emily hasn’t had time to tidy it up yet.  <sub>[v2 c25 P55](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0055)</sub>
